title: fix(plugin-audit, cli): isolate audit sealer faults per chain; os serve hands its crypto provider to an app-supplied AuditPlugin
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DXuamRUC67fx2TTYrFfyuSH)_

Part of #31908 (slice P4b1; seat ruling 6884540128 items 2 and 3)

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## Maintainer quick read

- What changes: the audit sealer isolates faults per chain. When a canonical rule refuses one of a chain's rows, or one of a chain's checkpoints (its head included) is malformed, only that chain is skipped, and the other chains seal as usual. Each chain has its own cursor and resumes from its own oldest unsealed window. Past a window that holds a skipped chain, `sealed_through` stops advancing. A lock lapse or a signer, crypto or storage fault still aborts the object's whole pass. Also: when an app puts its own `AuditPlugin` in `plugins` without a `cryptoProvider`, `os serve` now hands it the host's crypto provider. It does this only for the real `AuditPlugin` class, and it never overrides an explicit provider.
- Why: before, one bad row stopped sealing for every chain of the object. And an app's own `AuditPlugin` (one added to turn on `readAudit`, for example) replaced the CLI's instance, got no crypto provider, and sealed nothing.
- Risk and rollback: verdicts and refusal reasons are unchanged, and every existing seal and verify pin passes as is. The PR adds one public method, `AuditPlugin.adoptHostCryptoProvider` (widening). The sealer pass is window-major, and `late` never sweeps a lagging chain. Both are pinned per seat ruling 6885452378, the precondition for the verifier's sealed-window rule, which lands in P4c. Rollback is a revert.
- Read first: in `sealer.ts`, `run`, `cursorOf`, `skip`, `writeChains` and the catch in `readWindow`. In `serve.ts`, the `handHostCryptoToAppAuditPlugin` line inside the stack plugins loop. In `audit-plugin.ts`, `adoptHostCryptoProvider`.
- Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run src/audit-seal/audit-seal-sealer.test.ts src/audit-plugin.test.ts`. Expect 2 files and 65 tests, all green.
- Needed from you: nothing. The seat lands it.

## What changes

1. **S4, per-chain isolation (seat ruling 6884540128 item 2).** `sealer.ts`:
   - Only a chain-local fault skips a chain: a row a canonical rule refuses (`CanonicalFormError` while reading the row), or a malformed checkpoint of that chain (`SignedBodyError`/`CanonicalFormError` while reading it back: its head in `headOf`, a lister in the late re-count, a lister in `listedIn`, or its `window_start` while the cursors are read). The skipped chain stays out for the rest of the pass; every other chain is sealed. Lock lapse, signer, crypto-provider and storage faults (and the Q6 coordinate bound) still throw out of the object's pass, as before.
   - Each chain has its own cursor: the window after its last `window` checkpoint at or past the object's floor (the stored `sealed_through`, before which every chain is complete). A row is `late` only before its own chain's cursor; at or past it the window pass seals it as `window`. So a skipped chain (or one a stopped pass left) resumes from its own oldest unsealed window as `window` checkpoints. This replaces the object-wide `lastWindow` / `resumed` pair.
   - `sealed_through` on every `window` checkpoint is `min(window start, earliest window a skipped chain leaves unsealed)`, never below the stored floor. So it never passes a window that has a skipped chain.
   - The window walk starts at the floor. A window that only re-reads chains already sealed (or skipped) past it does not count toward `MAX_WINDOWS_PER_PASS`, so a stuck chain cannot stall the others behind the cap.
   - Each skipped chain is reported once at `error` per cause per hour, naming the object, the chain, the fault (code and reason, never a statement) and the window it is unsealed from. A chain sealed again is forgotten.
2. **App-supplied AuditPlugin (seat ruling 6884540128 item 3).**
   - `audit-plugin.ts`: new `adoptHostCryptoProvider(provider, { armSealer })`. It takes the provider only when the instance was composed with no `cryptoProvider`, so an explicit one is never overridden. `armSealer: false` (a one-shot boot) keeps the sealer off. `true` leaves the instance's own `armSealer` standing, so an app's `armSealer: false` is never turned on. Kept in private fields; the app's options object is not mutated.
   - `packages/cli/src/utils/app-audit-plugin-host-crypto.ts`: `handHostCryptoToAppAuditPlugin` hands over only to `instanceof` the real class, as this host loads it. A same-named lookalike is never touched. It never throws.
   - `serve.ts`: the class is loaded once, best-effort, ahead of the stack `plugins` loop. Each entry is handed `() => hostCrypto?.provider` and `!migrateAndExit` (the same provider function and one-shot posture as the 5d instance and the `requires: ['audit']` resolver) right before `kernel.use`. Boot is never refused. An instance left with no provider keeps D3's once-at-`error` report from its sealer.

Out of scope, untouched: S7, the item-5 DB session lock, verify's bootStack crypto (item 4, P4c), any `lifecycle.seal` default, expiry amendments, objectql lifecycle, `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `.github/workflows/**`.

## Tests

Tests first. Each new pin was run red before its fix.

- `audit-seal-sealer.test.ts`, new describe `per-chain isolation …`:
  - A refused row in org_b's 08:00 window. The deployment chain and org_a are sealed at 08:00, 09:00 and 10:00. org_b is not. Every `sealed_through` stays at 08:00. One `error` line names the object, `org:org_b`, `b1.payload` and "NOT being sealed".
  - Once the row is fixed, org_b resumes: `window` checkpoints at 08:00 (seq 0) and 09:00 (seq 1), not `late`. A third pass writes nothing.
  - A malformed head (org_b's checkpoint `root`). org_a is sealed at 09:00 and 10:00, both with `sealed_through` 09:00. org_b is skipped with one `error` line naming `root`.
  - A storage fault (`connection reset` on org_a's insert) still stops the whole object: nothing is stored, and one object-level `error` line. This one is green before and after; it preserves the abort.
  - Verify stays loud: `verifyAuditLedger` over the first scenario answers `ok: false`, with totals `unmodified: 2, late: 2, unsealed: 2`. This is the verdict `os audit verify` exits 1 on.
  - Window-major (seat ruling 6885452378): org_a writes every hour for 30 hours, which is more windows than one pass seals, and org_b writes only at hours 0, 11, 23 and 29. After pass 1, both chains' newest `window` checkpoint is at 23:00. After pass 2, both are at 29:00, and there is no `late` checkpoint. It was green at first run, so no code change was needed: the pass is one loop over windows that seals every due chain under one shared budget. Giving org_b its own budget turns it red (Verification).
  - No late sweep (seat ruling 6885452378): org_x is skipped at 08:00 while org_a seals 08:00 and 09:00. In pass 2, org_x recovers into `window` checkpoints at 08:00 (seq 0) and 09:00 (seq 1), and the only `late` checkpoint is org_a's own late row at 08:00. It was green at first run, so no code change was needed. Restoring the old every-chain late rule turns it red (Verification).
- `audit-plugin.test.ts`, new describe: takes the host provider when none was composed, and the sealer seals under it. Never overrides an explicit one. A one-shot host keeps the sealer off, and an app's `armSealer: false` stands. A host with no provider composes none, so the sealer is built without crypto and reports at `error`.
- `cli/src/utils/app-audit-plugin-host-crypto.test.ts`: the real class with no provider is fed. An explicit provider is not replaced. A same-named lookalike with an `adoptHostCryptoProvider` of its own is never called. The class missing or no plugin feeds nothing. A one-shot host disarms the sealer.
- `serve-audit-registration.contract.test.ts`: every existing assertion is kept. New: the hand-over call (exact spelling, with `() => hostCrypto?.provider` and `!migrateAndExit`) sits inside the stack `plugins` loop before `await kernel.use(pluginToLoad);`, and the real class is loaded ahead of the loop.

## Acceptance notes

- **Ruled: verify for a window where the skipped chain is the only chain.** The verifier today reads a window as sealed when a trusted `window` checkpoint names it, or when the window ends at or before the highest `sealed_through`. Ruling item 2 holds `sealed_through` at the skipped window. So if no other chain sealed that window, the skipped chain's rows there get no verdict. Seat ruling 6885452378 (option A) closes this in P4c: a window is also sealed when it starts at or before the highest `window_start` among trusted `window` checkpoints. The ADR-0154 D3 line is in #33489. Its two preconditions, a window-major pass and `late` never sweeping a lagging chain, are pinned in this PR (Tests).
- **A row whose `created_at` will not parse, when it is the oldest row of a span**, is met by the window walk's `firstRowAt` before any chain is read. That still stops the object's pass, as before. In `readWindow` the same fault skips only its chain.
- **Cost while a chain is stuck.** Each pass walks from the floor, so it re-reads the windows other chains already sealed past it until the stuck chain is fixed. This is bounded by how long the chain stays stuck. The cursor read fetches the `window` checkpoints at or past the floor. review#3 S1: bounding this re-walk is carried to P4b2.
- **A separately installed copy of `@objectstack/plugin-audit`** in the app is a different class from the one the host loads, so an instance of it is treated as a lookalike and is not fed. Its sealer reports the missing provider at `error`.
- **`OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1` with an app AuditPlugin that composed its own provider** arms its sealer, as before. The ruling feeds only instances with no provider, so this PR does not touch them.
- **Stacked on P4a (#33476).** Base is `claude/area-A2-31908-p4a`; the area thread retargets it to `main` once #33476 merges.
